step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture depicts Skyscanner's Kubernetes cluster running on AWS EC2 Spot Instances. First, an external rectangle represents the 80 million unique users. A prominent box labeled 'KBS CA' (Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler) is shown, which, based on the transcript, is a custom application running on EC2 instances responsible for managing the cluster's scaling. Two distinct 'ASG' (Auto Scaling Group) icons are shown, which correspond to the AWS AutoScaling service. The grid of smaller red squares within dashed Availability Zone boundaries represents the EC2 worker nodes for the Kubernetes cluster. Arrows indicate inbound user traffic to the 'KBS CA' node (following the visual primary ground truth, despite transcript suggesting an LB to nodes), and control plane interactions from 'KBS CA' to the Auto Scaling Groups, which then manage the EC2 worker nodes. A feedback loop from EC2 metadata to 'KBS CA' is also visually represented.

graph.name: Skyscanner Kubernetes Cluster on EC2 Spot Instances
graph.notes: Skyscanner's production Kubernetes clusters running 100% on EC2 Spot Instances across multiple regions and Availability Zones. The architecture leverages diversified Auto Scaling Groups and a custom Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler to handle spot instance terminations and manage the desired node count effectively for high-scale, cost-optimized operations.

nodes.name: Skyscanner Users

nodes.name: KBS Cluster Autoscaler
nodes.notes: A custom application (Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler) running on an EC2 instance, responsible for manipulating the desired count of EC2 instances within the Auto Scaling Groups. It processes instance metadata for termination notices and coordinates node draining.

nodes.name: Kubernetes Node ASG 1
nodes.notes: An Auto Scaling Group for Kubernetes worker nodes. It spans multiple Availability Zones and provides diversification of instance types (e.g., C3s, C4s, C5s, M4s, R3s) to enhance resilience when running 100% on Spot Instances.

nodes.name: Kubernetes Node ASG 2
nodes.notes: A second Auto Scaling Group for Kubernetes worker nodes, further contributing to the diversification of instance types and Spot capacity pools for increased stability and cost savings.

nodes.name: Kubernetes Worker Nodes
nodes.notes: A fleet of 120-130 EC2 Spot Instances (e.g., C5, C4, M5, C8X, C9X class types) distributed across multiple Availability Zones. These instances host the Kubernetes pods and services. One instance is visually marked for termination, illustrating the Spot termination handling.

edges.notes: Inbound user queries and traffic enter the Kubernetes cluster, as depicted by the visual arrow pointing to the 'KBS CA' node (acknowledging that typical data flow would involve a Load Balancer to worker nodes directly).
